text:
Ben: heads up — onboarding ACME edge today wants a committed GPU pool in eu-west-2. they quoted 120 rps (avg prompt ~300 tokens) and asked what commit we should propose. also noticed last month's dedicated invoice had ~12% unexplained overage. :grimacing:
Sara: for quick sizing i usually convert RPS -> tokens/sec -> GPU-seconds. rough calc: 120 rps * 300 tokens = 36k tokens/s -> with our perf profile on A100-80GB that's ~0.9 GPU-seconds/s (ballpark). so ~1 full GPU for steady, but add buffer for peaks. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Omar: the invoice overage might be unrelated to commit sizing — last month we had several failed preemptible fallbacks that got billed as on-demand. billing-bot attached a line item: `eu-west-2 transient reclaim charges` (see billing export). could be double-counting on the consolidation script.
Lina: agree with Sara for baseline. for contracts i recommend commit = steady * 1.5 and guaranteed floor = steady * 1.2. that buys headroom without overcommitting. also propose a burst band (pay-as-you-go) for 20% extra.
Ben: @Omar can you paste the billing export snippet? need to reconcile before we promise numbers.
Omar: here — paging the query I ran:
```
SELECT service, region, SUM(cost) as cost
FROM `billing.redwood.commit_month`
WHERE month = '2026-02' AND labels.pool = 'dedicated-eu-west-2-acme'
GROUP BY service, region
ORDER BY cost DESC
```
Omar: result showed ~€4.2k attributed to `compute.googleapis.com/instances/preemptible` and €3.9k to `compute.googleapis.com/instances` (on-demand). the preemptible->on-demand transitions look like the cause.
Sara: that explains the 12%. for sizing contract wording we should include a clause: "measured commit applies to sustained throughput measured at 95th percentile over billing window; transient preemption-driven fallbacks billed separately." keeps expectations clear.
Sai: quick simulation request: can someone run a cost model for commit = 1.5x steady vs commit = 2x steady, with burst band enabled (20%) and expected p95 tails? i can run the throughput sim if someone gives me historical RPS distribution for ACME test run.
Ben: i've uploaded a 72h sample from their integration tests to the shared bucket: gs://redwood-test-data/acme/commitsample-72h.csv — contains rps and avg token lengths.
Lina: i'll run the sim and post results in ~2h. if we go with 1.5x commit for the contract, recommended invoice guardrails: commit reconciliation window = 30d, buffer credit smoothing over 7d, and a one-time onboarding alignment credit to cover initial variance.
billing-bot: Notice: invoice reconciliation task #I-324 updated — assigned to @Omar.
Ben: action items: 1) @Omar reconcile preemptible fallbacks with billing export and confirm if our consolidation script over-attributed costs. 2) @Lina run throughput/cost sim on that 72h sample and post recommended commit bands + expected monthly cost delta. 3) @Sai validate SLA wording for commit measurement (p95 vs p99). 4) i'll draft contract language and share with legal.
Sara: FYI link to the dedicated commit playbook: https://redwood.internal/docs/dedicated-commit-playbook — has templates for the smoothing clause and burst band phrasing.
Ben: thanks team — let's try to get recon + sims done before EOD so sales can move the PO along. :pray:
